reason: The cited evidence shows that grain refinement increases strength (E1, E2) and that deformation mechanisms differ between coarse and ultrafine grains (E3), but none of the passages provide direct evidence for a screw-to-edge dislocation transition or for grain boundary sliding as the softening mechanism. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: Coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi deforms primarily by screw dislocation glide
Ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi deforms primarily by edge dislocation glide
A transition in dominant dislocation type governs the increase in hardness/strength with grain refinement
Below a critical nanoscale grain size (~10–50 nm), grain boundary sliding causes inverse Hall–Petch softening
